cwU_0WWeNZ4.title: If Voyager Needs 75,000 Years, How Far Is the Nearest Star?
cwU_0WWeNZ4.description:
How Far Is the Nearest Star?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5AdqQsnnys

Voyager 1 leaves the solar system at about seventeen kilometres every second. At that speed, reaching the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, would take about 75,000 years.

Sources: NASA JPL Voyager Mission Status (Voyager 1 heliocentric speed ~17 km/s) · Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023 (A&A 674, A1), Proxima Centauri at 4.24 light-years.

Pictures: NASA/JPL-Caltech Voyager imagery (PIA17049, PIA14111), NASA SDO solar imagery, and ESO Paranal night-sky time-lapses (CC BY 4.0), alongside AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/JPL-Caltech; NASA SDO; ESO.
